options.purpose: A voluntary bill check could help households find concessions, billing mistakes, avoidable fees and better offers. Any claimed saving would include the cost of changing providers.
options.redlandsAdaptation: Residents could access bill checks through existing library and community channels, supported by secure document handling and a dated referral guide. Participation and any initial case checks would require the household’s consent.
options.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek council support for accessible bill-check assistance through libraries and community partners. Document handling and referrals would be based on residents’ consent.

roleContext.title: What the mayor and council can do
roleContext.html:
The mayor chairs council meetings, speaks for council and has specific responsibilities for providing direction to the chief executive officer (CEO). The elected council votes on policy and budgets. The CEO manages day-to-day services and staff. Mayoral directions must stay within the Act and council’s decisions, including limits relating to staff appointments, discipline and unlawful conduct. Local Government Act, sections 12, 13, 104 and 170; Redland roles and responsibilities.

Who is involvedHow the mayoral role can help
Council services and facilitiesBuild support for policy, budgets, service improvements and decisions made by council.
State and federal governmentsBring people together, make submissions, seek funding and represent a council position that has been agreed.
Neighbouring councilsInvite shared learning, services, purchasing, mentoring or funding proposals. Each council decides its involvement.
Businesses and community organisationsListen to local needs and ideas, connect willing partners and support fair routes to grants, leases or contracts.
Luke’s projects and Strange But TruePut the public purpose first and use independent assessment and the applicable interest rules for any related transaction.

These options use a one-year planning horizon. The electoral term follows Queensland election law. Local government election guide.

roleContext.title: Public benefit and independent decisions
roleContext.html:
Writing an idea does not by itself settle a conflict-of-interest question. The actual decision and the officeholder’s financial and non-financial interests matter. Declaring an interest does not automatically allow someone to keep taking part in that decision. Local Government Act; registers of interests guidance.

The proposals begin with public purposes: lower avoidable costs, useful skills, reliable services, community connection and fair access. Council could compare ways to meet those purposes using clear criteria. A decision that could benefit Luke, Strange But True, his work or equipment, or an organisation he later establishes or joins would need the applicable interest process and independent advice before his participation.

Personal and Strange But True accounts and information would remain separate from council. General business support and a live tender have different rules. Council’s tender guidance explains the limits on contact with councillors. Any licence, donation, loan or use of Luke’s equipment would need clear terms and independent handling where interests arise. Council tender guidance.

Discussions would make clear whether Luke is speaking personally, for an organisation or on behalf of an agreed council position.

roleContext.title: Digital capability and council services
roleContext.html:
Personal AI, community learning, Verse Box, C-hours and public digital models connect with council’s responsibilities for services, information and privacy. The project introductions and names guide explain these terms. Council already has a Digital Transformation Portfolio, with existing systems, contracts and service responsibilities to take into account. Council’s digital program.

Joyful Responsible Abundance explains the wider goal: more people with the means to act and benefit. Preparing for possible superintelligence in 2027 or 2028 involves skills, privacy, reliable services, purchasing, access and partnerships. The timing is uncertain. The Sovereign Capacity Lab develops the related scenarios. Announced investment plans and money already spent remain different measures.
